locator: Sections C, D, M, N — the answer-format tag on every computation item

occurrences: C2, C3, D3, D4, M1–M6, N1–N4 (14 items across pp.1, 4)

locator: Section D item 4 (p.1) and Section M item 6 (p.4)
why: Both items are tagged "(decimal)" but their answers are whole numbers (7 and 9), and the companion's checked answers are plainly "7" and "9", so the tag contradicts the accepted answer and invites a student to write "7.0".

H1–H4 are bare equations/inequalities with no directive verb, and because H6 and H7 in the same section say "Graph …", the student cannot tell whether items 1–4 are to be solved or graphed — the companion's checked answers ("x = 11", "x > 5") show "Solve" was intended.

Every heading capitalises the short function words ("Of", "And"), the signature of a mechanical title-casing pass rather than a deliberate style, and it reads wrong in a student-facing document.
